sentences.text: Nothing happened in any sense that anybody could have filmed.
There were no ants in the house in the morning.

Mariana went in at seven and the room was exactly as she had left it, cold, with the window open, and there was nothing on the sill and nothing on the floor and nothing on the wall, and she shut the window and went and had breakfast.
Her mother came down at half past.
She looked at the window, which Mariana had shut, and at Mariana, and said good morning, and put the kettle on.
She had not slept properly since about August and she looked it and she was, that morning, ordinary.
And the thing that Mariana noticed, over the following four or five days, was not that the argument had stopped.
It was that nobody was avoiding anything.
That was what had been in the house since March: a shape everybody was walking around.
She had not known it was there until it was not, in the way you do not know a fridge is running.

The phone went from Lisbon on the Tuesday and her mother took it in the kitchen instead of going out to the yard, and talked about her uncle's daughter's school for eleven minutes, and put the phone down and made the tea and did not sit at the table afterwards with her hands flat on it.
Her father stopped being reasonable and went back to being ordinary, which was a considerable relief.
He argued with her about her phone on the Thursday, properly, at some volume, and Mariana went to bed almost cheerful.
Mariana did not tell anybody what she had done, and she did not feel guilty, and for about two years she thought she had got away with something clean.
She told her grandmother, in a manner of speaking, at the grave, in the February after, which she is aware is not the same as telling anybody.
